summary: Hoyo Watanabe (1933–2021) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University from circa 1952 to 1961. He spent his career at Rissho University as professor (c. 1974–2004), Dean of Buddhist Studies (attested 1984–1985), and special honorary professor (c. 2004–2021).
Hozen Seki (1903–1991) was a Buddhist studies figure who founded the American Buddhist Academy. He also served as resident minister at the New York Buddhist Church (attested 1998).

Hrachia Adjarian (1876–1953) was a linguist and scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the Faculty of Arts of Paris and Strasbourg, under Heinrich Hübschmann and Antoine Meillet. His teaching career included posts at Aramiyan School, Sanasarian College, and Yerevan State University.

Hrishikesh Terdalkar works in computational linguistics and Indology. He completed his PhD at the Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur under Arnab Bhattacharya, having also studied under Pralay Manna and Sowmya Krishnapur, and held a post at IIT Kanpur (attested 2023–2024).

Hsiang-Kuang Chou was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teacher Sivananda Saraswati. He served as Lecturer at the University of Delhi, Professor at the University of Allahabad, Lecturer at LBSNAA, and Chancellor of Yoga-Vedanta Forest Academy.

Hsiao-Lan Hu worked in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. After completing a PhD at Temple University, Hu served as associate professor of Religious Studies and Women's and Gender Studies at the University of Detroit Mercy (attested 2017).

Hsing Yun (1927–2023) was a Buddhist leader and scholar who studied under Zhikai, Ruoshun, Zhikang, and Yinshun. He served as abbot of Fo Guang Shan (c. 1967–1985), founded Fo Guang Shan and University of the West, and held a post at Chinese Culture University.
Hsiu-hui Ji is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed an MA at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin (attested 2009).
Hsu Yun (1840–1959) was a Buddhist master and scholar who studied under Changkai, Miaolian, and Yaocheng. In 1953, he founded the Buddhist Association of China and served as its honorary president.

Hsu-feng Lee is a Buddhist studies scholar. Lee earned a master's degree at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies under Huimin and a PhD at the University of Sydney under Mark Allon (attested 2017).

Hsuan Hua (1918–1995) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Chang Zhi and Hsu Yun. He founded the Dharma Realm Buddhist Association, the Buddhist Text Translation Society, and the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, where he served as abbot (c. 1976–1995).
Hsueh-li Cheng (born 1939) is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He held academic posts at Ohio University and the University of Hawaiʻi at Hilo (c. 1974–2014).

Hu Shih (1891–1962) was a philosopher and Sinologist who studied at Cornell and Columbia under John Dewey and Kaiten Nukariya. He served as chancellor of Peking University (1946–1948) and president of Academia Sinica (1957–1962).

Huabei Tan specializes in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. Tan pursued a PhD at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies under the supervision of Medawachchiye Dhammajothi (attested 2026).

Huai-Chin Nan (1918–2012) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Sinology who studied under Huanxian Yuan. He taught at the Republic of China Military Academy, National Chengchi University, Fu Jen Catholic University, and Chinese Culture University.

Huaiyu Chen (born 1974) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. Chen earned a master's at Peking University under Xinjiang Rong and a doctorate under Stephen F. Teiser, later serving as assistant professor at Arizona State University (c. 2007–2013).

Huanhuan He works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He has held positions at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, Zhejiang University, the University of Tokyo, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
Huawen Bai (1930–2021) was a scholar in Sinology and Buddhist studies. After studying at Peking University from circa 1951 to 1955, he served as a professor there from circa 1955 to 1996.

Hubert Decleer (1940–2021) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at KU Leuven under Étienne Lamotte. He served as academic director and senior faculty advisor at SIT Graduate Institute, and held visiting posts at Middlebury College and the University of Vienna.

Hubert Durt (1936–2018) was a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar who studied under Étienne Lamotte. He held posts at the École française d'Extrême-Orient, the Hōbōgirin Institute, the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
